comment: The nine engines of a website department, as data (engine_runtime.py): four work engines and five internal systems. EVERY engine names its start: the triggers that make it want to run (a new version of something, a post addressed to it, a time) and the blockers that hold it (gates of the internal systems, by id). An engine with no start is refused when the definitions are loaded, so every engine starts by the same rule. A step names its code, its prompt and its check; a name resolves only in the registry that ships with the app. born is the rung a step starts on; the rung it runs on is read from the department's ladder. EVERY step names a check: a definition with a step that has none is refused. coordination is the table Coordination is born with: who goes first when several engines are ready; a department keeps its own copy on its record, and only that copy is read. The journeys are canon's five (holding/website/native/products/cos/design-journeys.html): task, query, directive, feedback, new idea. WORDS: a step's name and an engine's description are shown on the screen, so they say function, the users' word; internal system is the word inside, for this comment, the documents and the code. KINDS: a department has a kind; its kind names its line, its artifacts, its born goal, done line and rules; Coordination's table is born with the kind's line. Root is a department of the kind root: its one engine, Setup, sets up a department the owner asked for, from the Library's templates, and the owner's stamp is its rule; there is one Root for one organisational structure. SHAPE: every unit, the steps of a work engine or of a handler, starts with a step by code and ends with a step by code; agents come between, so the input, the output and the least steps of any unit are known (founder, 2026-09-28). FRONT DOOR: the person speaks with Root; on a Root the owner's words arrive with the word front, and Root's Identity hears them, finds the department they are about (the chip, a name in the words, or the only child) and hands them on as a post from Root to that department's Identity, whose answers come back onto Root's board; a stamp, a refusal, Stop and Start go the same way (founder, 2026-09-28: one point of entry; the user always speaks with the root). LOST: a request of the owner's, or one Root handed on, that nobody answered inside its bound is closed by Coordination, which tells Identity (word lost); Identity says it back to the person and asks for the words again, so nothing said at the front door dies unseen (ER-9, found live 2026-09-28). TEMPLATES (TPL-1, founder 2026-09-29: a department is a skeleton; its functions, engines and artifacts come from Library templates matched to the use case, else the default): the work engines are not in this file; they are the Library's engine templates (engine-templates/<slug>.json, one per engine, each with a use case) and the runtime assembles the definitions from them. A kind is a department template: its use case, its line of engines, its artifacts, its functions' template (function-templates/<function>/<functions_template>.json), its born goal, done line and rules. Root's Setup picks the kind whose use case fits the owner's words, else default; the department's record carries the engines and artifacts it was born with, and everything reads the record. ENGINES FROM IDEAS (TPL-1 slice 2, founder 2026-09-29: the engines are created by the department's own functions): an idea the owner floats is shaped and parked by Adaptation, which then offers the engine it asks for (a Library template whose use case fits, else one shaped from Do with the idea as its instruction) to Priority; Priority prices it; Identity puts it to the owner; on the stamp Identity adds it to the record and Coordination's line, and a shaped engine is born into the Library with made_by; it then starts on its own trigger. REGISTRATION (PRD M4.1): Root records the plan that Priority said yes to and that passed Root's check (the ledger's workflow.registered); Coordination and Priority act on that record, each in a handler of its own on the fixed trigger 'an engine is born' (word born), run in place on the code rung: Coordination writes its own table, the line and a slot for each engine (coord.table), and Priority gives each new engine its limit (priority.grant). The same two handlers run when the owner stamps an engine an idea asked for. Posted on the board, the word born carries the same item ({engines, version, full}, or {grow, before}; engine_runtime.BORN_FIELDS), and a born word that names no engine of the department changes nothing. Root writes neither, and the engines a plan names come from Adaptation, never from Root. REQUIRED (PRD M4.4, Q12): a kind may mark engines of its line required; a plan that leaves one out does not pass Root's check, and a counter of Priority's that drops one goes to Identity as a conflict. When Root's check sends a plan of such a kind back, Adaptation takes the Library's line again, with the engines the kind requires, and does not reshape it: a shaped line is made of names new to the Library, so it can never carry one. The website kind's Check is required, because it enforces the owner's rules; no other engine is mandatory. THE LAYERS (PRD amendment A1): the five functions' engines are not in this file either. Each is its layer's recipe, layers/<layer>/v1.json (the same objects, moved byte for byte), which the runtime assembles before the Library's templates, so a version of a layer brings its recipe and its bodies together; what each layer holds, hears and sends is the interface, layer_schema.py. This file keeps the kinds, the edges, Coordination's born table and the journeys, and engines stays empty.
